items.title: Project skeleton & CI
items.description: Architect picks the stack (expected: TypeScript, zero runtime deps, built-in or dev-only test runner) and records it in ADR-0001, including the supported Kilo version range and the layout under backend/ (plugin single file, validation tooling, installers, provisioning). Senior BE creates a minimal plugin stub and one smoke test. CI releaser wires scripts/ci.sh and GitHub Actions to a green pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: Given a clean checkout, When `bash scripts/ci.sh` is run, Then it exits 0 and the output shows the backend package's type-check and test steps were executed (not the 'no packages yet' path).

Given the repository, When docs/architecture/ADR-0001-tech-stack.md is read by an automated check, Then the file exists and contains sections for language/runtime, test runner, supported Kilo version range, and the zero-runtime-dependency single-file plugin constraint (FR-11).

Given the backend package, When the test suite runs, Then a smoke test imports the single plugin source file (e.g. backend/plugin/azdo-remote-config.ts) and asserts it exports a plugin function that, when invoked with a minimal fake Kilo context, returns an object exposing a `config` hook.
Given backend/package.json, When an automated check inspects it, Then the `dependencies` field is absent or empty (only devDependencies are allowed).
Given a push or pull request to main, When the GitHub Actions CI workflow runs, Then it executes `bash scripts/ci.sh` (verifiable by a check that .github/workflows/ci.yml invokes scripts/ci.sh).
Given the plugin stub, When its `config` hook is invoked with a config object, Then it resolves without throwing and leaves the object unchanged (no-op until F-features land).

items.title: Plugin: JSONC parser
items.description: FR-4 / AC-5. Pure, exported function (e.g. `parseJsonc(text: string): unknown`) inside the single plugin file backend/plugin/azdo-remote-config.ts. Strips line/block comments and trailing commas outside strings, then JSON.parse. Zero runtime deps (FR-11). Not yet wired into the config hook (F-006).
acceptance_criteria: Given JSONC with `//` line comments and `/* */` block comments (including a multi-line block comment and a comment at end of file without trailing newline), When parsed, Then the result deep-equals the same document without comments.
Given JSONC with trailing commas in objects and arrays (including nested and with whitespace/comments between the comma and the closing bracket), When parsed, Then it parses to the expected object.
Given string values containing `https://host/path`, `/* not a comment */` and a literal `,}` sequence, When parsed, Then each string value is preserved exactly.

Given strings containing escaped quotes (`\"`) and escaped backslashes (a string ending in an escaped backslash, e.g. JSON source `"C:\\"`) followed by `//`, When parsed, Then string boundaries are respected and content is preserved.

Given invalid JSONC (unterminated string, unterminated block comment, or malformed JSON), When parsed, Then an Error with a descriptive message is thrown and the input text is not echoed in full in the message.

Given the Appendix A example from VISION.md, When parsed, Then provider.bifrost.options.baseURL equals `https://bifrost.yourcompany.internal/v1` and provider.bifrost.models has keys `azure/gpt-5` and `azure/gpt-5-mini`.
Given the plugin package after the change, When `bash scripts/ci.sh` (including the FR-11 lint) runs, Then it exits 0 and backend/package.json still has no runtime `dependencies`.

items.title: Plugin: {env:} and {file:} placeholder resolution
items.description: FR-5 / AC-8. Pure helper exposed as `__internals.resolvePlaceholders` (ADR-0002 seam) inside the single plugin file backend/plugin/azdo-remote-config.ts. Recursively resolves `{env:VAR}` and `{file:path}` placeholders in the parsed shared config and returns `{ value, unresolved }` where `unresolved` is a list of placeholder names (never values). Environment, home directory and file reader are injectable for tests (defaults: process.env, os.homedir(), fs.readFileSync). Not yet wired into the config hook (F-006). Zero runtime deps (FR-11).
acceptance_criteria: Given `{"x": "{env:SET_VAR}"}` and an injected env with SET_VAR=abc, When `__internals.resolvePlaceholders` runs, Then result.value.x equals `abc` and result.unresolved is empty.

Given `{"x": "{env:MISSING}", "y": 1}` with MISSING unset, When resolved, Then key x is absent from result.value (not present as undefined/empty), y equals 1, and result.unresolved contains exactly `env:MISSING`.
Given `{"x": "pre-{env:MISSING}-post"}` with MISSING unset, When resolved, Then x equals `pre--post` and result.unresolved contains `env:MISSING`.

Given `{"x": "{file:~/secret.txt}"}` and secret.txt containing `  s3cret\n` under an injected fake home directory, When resolved, Then x equals `s3cret` (trimmed) and the file read targeted `<home>/secret.txt` (`~/` expanded).

Given `{file:...}` that cannot be read (missing path, a directory, or a reader that throws with the file contents in its error message), When resolved, Then the key is dropped, result.unresolved contains `file:<path as written>`, and no returned or thrown value contains the file contents or the reader's error text.

Given placeholders nested in objects and arrays (e.g. `{"a":{"b":["{env:SET_VAR}","{env:MISSING}","keep"]}}`), When resolved, Then nested values follow the same rules, an array element that is only an unresolved placeholder is removed from the array (giving `["abc","keep"]`), and non-string values (numbers, booleans, null) and strings without placeholders are returned unchanged.

Given any input object, When resolved, Then the input object is not mutated, own keys `__proto__`, `constructor` and `prototype` in the input do not pollute Object.prototype, and a string containing multiple placeholders (`{env:A}/{env:B}`) resolves each one.

Given the plugin package after the change, When `bash scripts/ci.sh` (including the FR-11 lint) runs, Then it exits 0, backend/package.json has no runtime `dependencies`, and the only new export surface is the `resolvePlaceholders` key on `__internals`.

items.title: Plugin: in-place merge with defaults/enforce modes
items.description: FR-6 / AC-6 / AC-7. Pure helper exposed as `__internals.mergeConfig(target, shared, mode)` (ADR-0002 seam) inside the single plugin file backend/plugin/azdo-remote-config.ts. Deep-merges the (already parsed and placeholder-resolved) shared config into Kilo's resolved config object, mutating `target` in place. Plain objects are merged recursively; arrays and scalars are leaf values whose conflict is decided by mode (`defaults`: local wins; `enforce`: shared wins); a key absent locally is added from shared in both modes. Top-level `$schema` and `plugin` in the shared config are ignored. Any `apiKey` key at any depth in the shared config is never applied (local apiKey always preserved; vision AC-6, FR-12). Values copied from shared are deep-cloned so target never aliases shared. An unrecognised mode is treated as `defaults` (conservative). Not yet wired into the config hook (F-006). Zero runtime deps (FR-11).
acceptance_criteria: Given local `{model:'a'}` and shared `{model:'b', small_model:'s'}`, When `__internals.mergeConfig` runs in `defaults` mode, Then target.model equals `a` and target.small_model equals `s` (shared-only keys are added).

Given local `{model:'a', provider:{bifrost:{options:{baseURL:'L'}}}}` and shared `{model:'b', provider:{bifrost:{options:{baseURL:'S'}}}}`, When merged in `enforce` mode, Then target.model equals `b` and target.provider.bifrost.options.baseURL equals `S`; and When merged in `defaults` mode, Then both local values are kept (AC-7).

Given local `provider.bifrost.options.apiKey = 'sk-bf-local'` and a shared provider.bifrost block whose options contain `apiKey: 'sk-bf-shared'` plus `baseURL`, When merged in `defaults` and in `enforce` mode, Then apiKey still equals `sk-bf-local`, baseURL is merged per mode, and with a local config that has no apiKey the shared apiKey is not added (AC-6).

Given local keys absent from the shared file at top level and nested (e.g. `provider.other`, `provider.bifrost.options.headers`, `agent.x`), When merged in either mode, Then those keys and their values are unchanged.
Given a shared config with top-level `$schema` and `plugin`, When merged in either mode, Then the local `$schema` and `plugin` values are unchanged, and when absent locally they are not added.

Given a target object, When merged, Then the function mutates and keeps the same target reference (including existing nested object references such as target.provider), the shared input is not mutated, and mutating a nested object or array in shared after the merge does not change target.

Given arrays or type conflicts (local `instructions:['a']` vs shared `['b','c']`; local object vs shared string), When merged, Then arrays are replaced wholesale (never concatenated) and conflicts resolve by mode (`defaults` keeps local, `enforce` takes shared), and an unrecognised mode behaves as `defaults`.

Given a shared config parsed from JSON containing own keys `__proto__`, `constructor` or `prototype` at top level and nested, When merged, Then Object.prototype is not polluted and no such key alters target's prototype; and When `bash scripts/ci.sh` (including the FR-11 lint) runs, Then it exits 0, backend/package.json has no runtime `dependencies`, and the only new export surface is the `mergeConfig` key on `__internals`.

items.title: Plugin: settings resolution (options, env, defaults)
items.description: FR-1 / FR-8 (and the settings half of FR-3). Pure helper exposed as `__internals.resolveSettings(options, deps?)` (ADR-0002 seam) inside the single plugin file backend/plugin/azdo-remote-config.ts. Resolves org, project, repo, path, branch, mode, pat, timeoutMs with precedence: plugin option (non-empty string / finite number) > KILO_AZDO_* env var (KILO_AZDO_ORG, KILO_AZDO_PROJECT, KILO_AZDO_REPO, KILO_AZDO_PATH, KILO_AZDO_BRANCH, KILO_AZDO_MODE, KILO_AZDO_PAT, KILO_AZDO_TIMEOUT_MS) > built-in default (path `/kilo.jsonc`, branch `main`, mode `defaults`, timeoutMs 5000; org/project/repo/pat have no default). Returns `{ settings, missing, warnings }` where `missing` lists required setting names (org, project, repo) that are unset and `warnings` are fixed messages naming settings only, never values. Env is injectable (default process.env, own properties only). The AZDO_PAT / AZURE_DEVOPS_EXT_PAT fallback and the az token belong to F-005; logging through Kilo's logger is wired in F-006. Not yet wired into the server/config hook. Zero runtime deps (FR-11).
acceptance_criteria: Given options `{org:"opt"}` and an injected env with KILO_AZDO_ORG=env, When `__internals.resolveSettings` runs, Then settings.org equals `opt`; and Given no `branch` option and KILO_AZDO_BRANCH=dev, Then settings.branch equals `dev` (option > env precedence verified for each of org, project, repo, path, branch, mode, pat, timeoutMs).

Given no options (undefined) and an empty env, When settings resolve, Then path is `/kilo.jsonc`, branch is `main`, mode is `defaults`, timeoutMs is 5000, org/project/repo/pat are undefined, and `missing` deep-equals ["org","project","repo"].

Given mode `enforce` from options or from KILO_AZDO_MODE, When settings resolve, Then mode is `enforce`; and Given an invalid mode (e.g. `force`, `ENFORCE`, a number) from options or env, When settings resolve, Then mode is `defaults` and `warnings` contains an entry naming `mode`.

Given timeoutMs 3000 as an option number, or KILO_AZDO_TIMEOUT_MS=`2500` in env, When settings resolve, Then timeoutMs is 3000 or 2500 respectively; and Given a non-numeric, zero, negative, NaN, Infinity or non-integer value (option or env), When settings resolve, Then timeoutMs is 5000 and `warnings` contains an entry naming `timeoutMs`.

Given options that are null, an array, a string or a number, or option values of the wrong type (number for org, object for branch) or empty/whitespace-only strings, When settings resolve, Then no error is thrown and each such value is ignored so the env value or default applies; string values are trimmed, and a path without a leading `/` (e.g. `teams/a/kilo.jsonc`) is normalised to `/teams/a/kilo.jsonc`.

Given a `pat` option and KILO_AZDO_PAT both set, When settings resolve, Then settings.pat equals the option value; and Given any input containing a pat value (valid or wrongly typed), When `missing`, `warnings` and any thrown error are inspected, Then none of them contains the pat value.

Given inputs, When settings resolve, Then the options object and env are not mutated, an env created via Object.create({KILO_AZDO_ORG:"inh"}) does not supply org (own properties only), and own keys `__proto__`/`constructor`/`prototype` in options do not pollute Object.prototype or the returned settings.

Given the plugin package after the change, When `bash scripts/ci.sh` (including the FR-11 lint) runs, Then it exits 0, backend/package.json has no runtime `dependencies`, and the only new export surface is the `resolveSettings` key on `__internals`.

items.title: Plugin: Azure DevOps fetch and authentication
items.description: FR-2 / FR-3 / FR-8. Async helper exposed as `__internals.fetchRemoteConfig(settings, deps?)` (ADR-0002 seam) inside the single plugin file backend/plugin/azdo-remote-config.ts. Takes the output `settings` of `resolveSettings` (F-004, contract 0.5.0; `settings.pat` already covers the plugin option and KILO_AZDO_PAT) and fetches the shared file via the Azure DevOps Git Items API. Returns a discriminated result `{ ok: true, text }` or `{ ok: false, error }` where `error` is a fixed, value-free code/message (e.g. invalid-settings, auth-unavailable, timeout, http-<status>, too-large, bad-response, network); it NEVER throws or rejects (FR-10). Injectable deps: `fetch` (default globalThis.fetch), `env` (default process.env, own properties only), `runAz` (default: node:child_process execFile without a shell, bounded by timeoutMs), and timer/AbortController seams as the Architect sees fit. Request uses `Accept: application/json`; the file text is read from the JSON body's `content` string. Lone UTF-16 surrogates in settings (security low finding 1, cycle 0006) must be handled here: either an `isWellFormed()` guard via a contract amendment or catching URIError during URL building. Parsing, placeholder resolution, merge, cache and logging stay in F-006. Zero runtime npm deps (FR-11); Node built-ins only.
acceptance_criteria: Given settings {org:'my org', project:'plat form', repo:'kilo-config', path:'/teams/a b/kilo.jsonc', branch:'release/1', timeoutMs:5000} and a fake fetch, When `__internals.fetchRemoteConfig` runs, Then exactly one GET is sent to `https://dev.azure.com/{org}/{project}/_apis/git/repositories/{repo}/items` with org/project/repo percent-encoded as path segments and query parameters path, versionDescriptor.version=<branch>, versionDescriptor.versionType=branch, includeContent=true and api-version=7.1 (all values percent-encoded), with an `Accept: application/json` header; and Given a 200 response whose JSON body has `content` equal to a JSONC string, Then the result is `{ ok: true, text }` with text equal to that string byte-for-byte (not parsed).

Given PAT sources, When the request is built, Then the Authorization header is `Basic ` + base64(':' + pat) using the first available of: settings.pat (plugin option or KILO_AZDO_PAT, from resolveSettings), then injected env AZDO_PAT, then AZURE_DEVOPS_EXT_PAT (empty/whitespace-only values skipped, env read as own properties only); and in every PAT case the injected az runner is never invoked.

Given no PAT from any source, When fetching, Then the injected az runner is invoked once with arguments starting `account get-access-token --resource 499b84ac-1321-427f-aa17-267ca6975798` (no shell), the trimmed returned token is sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`; and Given the runner throws, exits non-zero, times out or returns empty output, Then no HTTP request is sent and the result is `{ ok: false }` with a fixed auth-unavailable error.

Given a fake fetch that never responds, When fetching with timeoutMs 50, Then the request's AbortSignal is aborted at the timeout and the result is `{ ok: false }` with a timeout error within a bounded time (no hang), and the default timeout when settings come from resolveSettings defaults is 5000 ms (FR-8).

Given a non-2xx response (e.g. 401, 404, 500), or a fetch that rejects with an error whose message contains the PAT, When fetching, Then the result is `{ ok: false }` and the error includes the HTTP status number for non-2xx responses, while no returned error contains the PAT, the bearer token, the Authorization header value or the underlying error's message.

Given a response larger than 1 MiB (declared by Content-Length or actual body length when the header is missing or lies), or a 200 body that is not JSON or lacks a string `content` field, When fetching, Then the result is `{ ok: false }` with a too-large or bad-response error and no oversized text is returned (cap enforced before any parsing; parseJsonc memory is about 50x input size).

Given settings with missing org/project/repo, or a value containing a lone surrogate (e.g. org `�`) that passed resolveSettings, When fetching, Then no URIError or other exception escapes, neither fetch nor the az runner is called, and the result is `{ ok: false }` with an invalid-settings error that names no values.

Given any input including hostile values (null/non-object settings or deps, throwing fetch, throwing env proxy), When `fetchRemoteConfig` runs, Then the returned promise always resolves (never rejects) and the settings/env objects are not mutated; and When `bash scripts/ci.sh` (including the FR-11 lint) runs, Then it exits 0, backend/package.json has no runtime `dependencies`, and the only new export surface is the `fetchRemoteConfig` key on `__internals`.

items.title: Plugin: cache, fallback, logging and never-crash wiring
items.description: FR-7 / FR-9 / FR-10 / AC-3 / AC-4 / AC-6 / AC-7 / AC-8 / AC-9, startup steps 2-6. Wire the shipped helpers (resolveSettings, fetchRemoteConfig, parseJsonc, resolvePlaceholders, mergeConfig) into the plugin's exported `config` hook inside the single file backend/plugin/azdo-remote-config.ts. Flow: resolve settings from plugin options + env; if `missing` is non-empty skip the fetch (log setting names only) and use the cache path; otherwise fetch; parse and validate the fetched text (root must be a plain object); on success write the cache, on any failure read the cache; resolve placeholders on the chosen config; merge in place with settings.mode. Cache: `<home>/.cache/kilo-azdo/remote-config.json`, holding the parsed shared config BEFORE placeholder resolution (PO decision: resolved {env:}/{file:} values may be secrets and must never be written to disk); directory created if missing; file mode 0600 on POSIX; written atomically (temp file + rename) so a crash never leaves a half-written cache; the cache content is validated on read exactly like fetched content. Logging goes through Kilo's logger with `service: azdo-remote-config` (Architect decides the exact Kilo logger API and keeps an injectable logger seam for tests); only fixed messages, setting names, error codes and placeholder names are logged, never values, and `settings` is never passed to the logger as an object. Trust boundary (cycle 0007 security info 4): the Architect records in an ADR which Kilo config layers may supply org/project/repo/path/pat and that fetched and cached content is treated as untrusted input (validated before merge; apiKey never applied, already enforced by mergeConfig). Deps (home dir, fs, fetch, env, runAz, logger) are injectable; tests never touch the real home directory or network. The Windows case-insensitive process.env note moved to T-012. Zero runtime npm deps (FR-11).
acceptance_criteria: Given complete settings in plugin options, a fake fetch returning a shared JSONC with comments and `{"model":"shared","small_model":"s","provider":{"bifrost":{"options":{"baseURL":"https://b/v1","apiKey":"sk-bf-shared"}}}}`, and a Kilo config `{model:'local', provider:{bifrost:{options:{apiKey:'sk-bf-local'}}}}`, When the plugin's `config` hook runs in `defaults` mode, Then the same config object is mutated in place with model `local`, small_model `s`, baseURL `https://b/v1` and apiKey `sk-bf-local`; and in `enforce` mode model becomes `shared` while apiKey stays `sk-bf-local` (AC-6, AC-7).

Given a successful fetch and a fake home directory without `.cache/kilo-azdo/`, When the hook runs, Then `<home>/.cache/kilo-azdo/remote-config.json` is created containing the parsed shared config with placeholders still unresolved (no resolved env/file value is written to disk), the write is atomic (temp file + rename), and on POSIX the file mode is 0600; and an info log with service `azdo-remote-config` states the remote source was used.

Given the fetch fails (e.g. timeout or http-500) and a valid cache file exists, When the hook runs, Then the cached config is placeholder-resolved and merged into the config, the cache is not overwritten, and a warn-level log with service `azdo-remote-config` names the fixed error code (AC-3).

Given the fetch fails and no cache exists, or the cache file is corrupt, not JSON, or has a non-object root, When the hook runs, Then the config deep-equals its original value, an error-level log is written with a fixed message, and a corrupt cache is never merged (AC-4).

Given resolved settings with `missing` non-empty, When the hook runs, Then neither fetch nor the az runner is called, the log names only the missing setting names (e.g. `org`), the cache fallback of the previous criteria applies, and each resolveSettings warning is logged at warn level; and Given fetched text that is invalid JSONC or whose root is not a plain object (array, string, number, null), When the hook runs, Then it is neither merged nor cached and the cache fallback applies.

Given a shared file containing `"x": "{env:MISSING}"` and `"y": "{env:SECRET_VAR}"` with SECRET_VAR set to `s3cr3t-value`, When the hook runs, Then config.x is not set, config.y is `s3cr3t-value`, and the logs name `env:MISSING` but contain neither `s3cr3t-value` nor any other placeholder value (AC-8).

Given a run with a PAT in plugin options, a bearer token returned by a fake az runner (PAT-less run), an `sk-bf-` apiKey in the local config and a resolved secret placeholder, across the success, cache-fallback and exception paths, When every argument of every logger call is captured and serialised (including util.inspect with showHidden), Then none contains any of those secret values, and the logger never receives the settings object (AC-9, FR-9).

Given each internal failure in turn (fetch dependency rejecting, parseJsonc throwing, unwritable cache directory, cache write throwing, logger throwing, a frozen Kilo config making mergeConfig throw TypeError, options null or non-object), When the hook runs, Then it resolves without throwing, any logged message is fixed text (never err.message), and Kilo's config is left either unchanged or fully merged (FR-10); and When `bash scripts/ci.sh` (including the FR-11 lint) runs, Then it exits 0, backend/package.json has no runtime `dependencies`, and docs/architecture contains an ADR stating which config layers may supply org/project/repo/path/pat and that fetched/cached content is validated as untrusted before merge.

items.title: Shared config repo: example kilo.jsonc and validation script
items.description: FR-12 / FR-13 / AC-13, plus cycle 0005 security follow-ups. Two deliverables for C1 (shared config repo): (a) an example shared config, e.g. backend/shared-config/kilo.jsonc, based on VISION Appendix A (Bifrost provider with baseURL and models, no apiKey, no secrets); (b) a zero-runtime-dependency validator CLI under backend/validator/ (ADR-0001 layout, Node >=22.18 built-ins only, run e.g. as `node backend/validator/validate-kilo-config.ts <file>...`), used later by the Azure Pipelines PR gate (F-008) and the template check (F-009). The validator must reuse the plugin's JSONC parser (`__internals.parseJsonc` or an Architect-approved import) rather than a second copy, and must NOT change the plugin's export surface. Rules: parse JSONC; root must be a plain object; check a vendored Kilo config schema subset (Architect defines it, pinned to SUPPORTED_KILO_RANGE, stored under backend/validator/); reject any `apiKey` key at any depth (key name compared case-insensitively); reject `sk-bf-` secret patterns in string values and comments without echoing the secret; reject own keys `__proto__`/`constructor`/`prototype`; warn on other Object.prototype member names (e.g. hasOwnProperty, toString), on `{file:}` paths that never resolve (relative, bare `~`, `~user`, UNC / `//host`), and on top-level `plugin` (ignored by the merge); optional `--allowed-hosts h1,h2` flag rejects provider `options.baseURL` values that are not https or whose host is not in the set. Exit codes (PO decision): 0 = valid (warnings allowed), 1 = validation errors in any file, 2 = usage or I/O error. Output names files, JSON paths and rule ids, never secret values. Tests live in backend/test/validator/ and are run by `bash scripts/ci.sh`.
acceptance_criteria: Given the shipped example shared config (e.g. backend/shared-config/kilo.jsonc, Appendix A content with comments and an https baseURL), When the validator CLI runs on it in a child process, Then it exits 0, reports the file as valid, and the parsed example has provider.bifrost.options.baseURL as a string and provider.bifrost.models keys `azure/gpt-5` and `azure/gpt-5-mini` and no `apiKey` anywhere.

Given files containing an `apiKey` key at top level, at `provider.bifrost.options.apiKey`, inside an array element, and spelled `APIKEY`, When validated, Then each run exits 1 and the output names the JSON path of the offending key (e.g. `provider.bifrost.options.apiKey`) and does not contain the key's value.

Given a file with the string `sk-bf-AbCdEf1234567890` as a nested value, inside a longer string, inside an array, or in a `//` or `/* */` comment, When validated, Then the run exits 1, the output names the JSON path (or the line number for a comment), and the output never contains `AbCdEf1234567890`.

Given invalid JSONC (unterminated string, unterminated block comment, malformed JSON) or a root that is an array, string, number or null, When validated, Then the validator exits 1 with a parse/shape error naming the file and no stack trace; and Given no file argument or a path that does not exist, When run, Then it exits 2 with a usage or I/O message.

Given files violating the vendored Kilo schema subset (`provider` not an object, `provider.bifrost` not an object, `provider.bifrost.options` or `provider.bifrost.models` not an object, `model` not a string), When validated, Then each exits 1 naming the JSON path; and an automated check confirms the vendored subset file exists under backend/validator/ and records the Kilo version range it was taken from.

Given a shared config whose `{file:}` placeholders use a relative path, bare `~`, `~user/x`, or a UNC / `//host/share` path, When validated, Then the run exits 0 (no other errors) and prints one warning per placeholder naming the JSON path and stating it will never resolve; and `{file:~/x}`, absolute paths and `{env:VAR}` produce no such warning.

Given own keys `__proto__`, `constructor` or `prototype` at any depth, When validated, Then the run exits 1 naming the path and Object.prototype is not polluted; Given keys `hasOwnProperty` or `toString`, Then a warning names the path; and Given `--allowed-hosts bifrost.yourcompany.internal`, When a provider `options.baseURL` is non-https, unparseable, or has another host, Then the run exits 1 naming the path, while without the flag no host error is raised.

Given two files where one is valid and one has an error, When the validator runs on both in one call, Then it exits 1 and reports a result for each file; and When `bash scripts/ci.sh` (including the FR-11 lint) runs, Then it exits 0, runs the validator tests under backend/test/validator/, backend/package.json has no runtime `dependencies`, and the plugin's export surface is unchanged.

items.title: Shared config repo: Azure Pipelines PR gate and branch policy setup
items.description: FR-13 / FR-14 / AC-13, C1 (shared config repo). Cycle 0015 PO: priority raised to 2 (critical path; F-015 depends on it). Two deliverables under backend/shared-config/ (the template of the C1 `kilo-config` repo; Architect fixes exact file names and records them in an ADR + contract, e.g. a new contracts/shared-config-repo.md): (a) `azure-pipelines.yml`, the PR validation pipeline: `trigger: none` (or main only), `pr` on branch main, installs/uses Node >= 22.18 (e.g. UseNode@1 / NodeTool@0, no npm install, zero runtime deps), and runs the F-007 validator CLI with `--allowed-hosts <host list>` (host list from a pipeline variable with a documented default; cycle 0009: host check is opt-in and ignores ports) over `kilo.jsonc` plus every `teams/*/kilo.jsonc` that exists (no teams directory, or an empty one, must not cause a usage error/exit 2); a non-zero validator exit fails the job. The validator needs `validator/` and `plugin/azdo-remote-config.ts` in the same relative layout plus a package.json with "type": "module" (ADR-0010): the Architect decides how C1 gets them (PO suggestion: a zero-dependency assemble/export script, e.g. `node backend/tools/assemble-shared-repo.ts <outdir>`, that writes the complete C1 repo tree: kilo.jsonc, azure-pipelines.yml, the policy script, the validator files, the plugin file and package.json, byte-identical copies, refusing a non-empty outdir) so the pipeline's exact command line is testable end to end. (b) A branch-policy script for the platform team (Architect picks bash or a zero-dependency Node .ts; it must run on macOS/Linux and Git Bash) that applies FR-14 to `main` with `az repos policy`: approver-count (minimum 1 reviewer, blocking), required-reviewer for the platform-team group, and build validation bound to the pipeline's build definition id (blocking). Inputs: org (URL or name), project, repository id or name, reviewer group id/descriptor, build definition id, all REQUIRED as flags; `--dry-run` prints the exact az commands without invoking az. It never takes a PAT/token as an argument (az login or AZURE_DEVOPS_EXT_PAT env only), never echoes env values, and passes each value as a single argv element (no eval / shell interpolation). PO decision: idempotency (detecting existing policies) is out of scope for this slice; the usage text states that re-running creates duplicate policies. Tests (node:test under backend/test/) inspect the YAML as text or with a tiny dev-only parser, run the pipeline's validator command in a temp copy/assembled tree, and run the policy script in child processes with a stub `az` on PATH that records argv; they never call real az, Azure DevOps or the network. The plugin file, its export surface, the validator rules/CLI behaviour, the installers and the personal config template are unchanged. Zero runtime npm deps (FR-11). Out of scope: per-team example files and team-specific validation behaviour (F-015).
acceptance_criteria: Given backend/shared-config/azure-pipelines.yml, When a test inspects it, Then it has a `pr` trigger including branch `main`, CI-push triggering is disabled or limited to main, it selects Node 22.18 or later, contains no `npm install`/`npm ci` step, and has a script step that invokes the validator CLI (`validate-kilo-config.ts`) with `--allowed-hosts` and the files `kilo.jsonc` and `teams/*/kilo.jsonc`.

Given the C1 repo tree in a temp directory (as assembled by the Architect's chosen mechanism) containing the example kilo.jsonc and no teams directory, When the pipeline's validator script step is executed in bash from the repo root with the default allowed-hosts value, Then it exits 0; and Given a `teams/payments/kilo.jsonc` that is valid, Then it exits 0 and the output reports both files.

Given the same temp C1 tree, When kilo.jsonc (or teams/x/kilo.jsonc) gains an `apiKey` field, an `sk-bf-AbCdEf1234567890` string, or a baseURL on a host not in the allowed-hosts list, When the pipeline's validator script step runs, Then it exits non-zero (failing the PR, AC-13) and the output never contains `AbCdEf1234567890`.

Given the C1 tree, When it is inspected, Then validator/validate-kilo-config.ts, validator/kilo-config-rules.ts, validator/kilo-schema-subset.json and plugin/azdo-remote-config.ts are byte-identical to the backend/ sources and their relative layout matches backend/, and a package.json with `"type": "module"` and no `dependencies` is present.

Given the branch-policy script with all required inputs and `--dry-run`, When executed with a stub az on PATH, Then it exits 0, the stub az is never invoked, and stdout lists exactly three `az repos policy` commands: `approver-count create` with `--minimum-approver-count 1` and `--blocking true`, `required-reviewer create` naming the supplied reviewer group, and `build create` naming the supplied build definition id with `--blocking true`, each scoped to `--branch main` and the supplied repository, org and project.

Given the branch-policy script without `--dry-run`, When executed with a recording stub az, Then az is invoked exactly three times with the same arguments as the dry-run output (each value as one argv element, so a value like `team; rm -rf x` or `$(id)` is passed literally and nothing else is executed), and Given the stub az fails on any call, Then the script stops at that call and exits non-zero with a fixed message naming the failing policy, without echoing az's output.

Given the branch-policy script with any required input missing, an empty value, an unknown flag, or a positional argument, When executed, Then it exits 2 with usage help that does not echo the offending value, and az is never invoked; and Given AZURE_DEVOPS_EXT_PAT set to a sentinel value on any path, Then the sentinel appears in no stdout/stderr, and the script accepts no flag for a PAT or token.

Given the repository after the change, When `bash scripts/ci.sh` (including the FR-11 lint) runs, Then it exits 0 and runs the new pipeline and policy-script tests, backend/package.json has no runtime `dependencies`, backend/plugin/azdo-remote-config.ts, backend/validator/*, backend/personal-config/kilo.jsonc and backend/installer/* are unchanged, and docs/architecture documents the C1 repo layout, the pipeline and the policy script's flags and exit codes.

items.title: Personal config template
items.description: FR-16 / FR-17, C3. Ship the personal config template matching VISION Appendix B as a JSONC file under backend/ (PO default: backend/personal-config/kilo.jsonc; Architect may pick another path under backend/ and record it). It is the file the installers (F-010/F-011) copy to `~/.config/kilo/kilo.jsonc`. Content: `$schema`, one `plugin` entry `["./azdo/azdo-remote-config.ts", {org, project, repo, path, branch, mode}]` with example values (contoso / platform / kilo-config / /kilo.jsonc / main / defaults; org, project and repo written explicitly because repo has no default since contract 0.5.0; no `pat` option, PAT and az login come from env/az per FR-3), and `provider.bifrost.options.apiKey` holding a placeholder (PO default `sk-bf-<your-virtual-key>`) that does NOT match the validator's SECRET_PATTERN. A comment states the file belongs in the global config directory only, never in a project directory (FR-17). The template legitimately contains `apiKey`, so it is NOT checked with the full shared-config rule set: tests reuse the F-007 validator library (`validateConfigText` from backend/validator/kilo-config-rules.ts) and filter its findings (secret-pattern must be absent; api-key and plugin-ignored are expected for this file). No change to the plugin file or its export surface, and no change to the validator's rules or CLI behaviour. Tests live under backend/test/ and run via `bash scripts/ci.sh`. Zero runtime npm deps (FR-11).
acceptance_criteria: Given the shipped template file, When it is read and parsed with the plugin's `__internals.parseJsonc`, Then it parses without error, the root is a plain object whose top-level keys are exactly `$schema`, `plugin` and `provider`, `$schema` equals `https://app.kilo.ai/config.json`, and the raw text contains a comment mentioning `~/.config/kilo/kilo.jsonc` and that the file must not be placed in a project directory (FR-17).

Given the parsed template, When `plugin` is inspected, Then it is an array with exactly one entry, that entry is a two-element array whose first element is `./azdo/azdo-remote-config.ts` and whose second element is an object with exactly the keys org, project, repo, path, branch and mode (no `pat`), each a non-empty string, with path starting with `/` and mode equal to `defaults` or `enforce`.

Given the template's plugin options, When passed to `__internals.resolveSettings` with an empty injected env, Then `missing` is empty, `warnings` is empty, and settings.org/project/repo/path/branch/mode equal the template's values (the template alone is a complete configuration).

Given the parsed template, When `provider` is inspected, Then its only key is `bifrost`, `provider.bifrost` has only the key `options`, `provider.bifrost.options` has only the key `apiKey`, and apiKey is a string that starts with `sk-bf-` but does not match the validator's exported `SECRET_PATTERN` (e.g. `sk-bf-<your-virtual-key>`), so no baseURL, models or other shared values are duplicated locally.

Given the template text, When validated with the F-007 library `validateConfigText`, Then there is no `secret-pattern` finding and no error finding other than the expected `api-key` rule; and Given a copy of the template text with the placeholder replaced by `sk-bf-AbCdEf1234567890`, When validated the same way, Then a `secret-pattern` finding is reported and no finding field contains `AbCdEf1234567890` (the check is not vacuous).

Given the template as the local Kilo config and the shipped shared example (F-007 backend/shared-config/kilo.jsonc) parsed with parseJsonc, When `__internals.mergeConfig` runs in `defaults` and in `enforce` mode, Then provider.bifrost.options.apiKey still equals the template placeholder, provider.bifrost.options.baseURL and the models `azure/gpt-5` and `azure/gpt-5-mini` are added from the shared file, and the local `plugin` and `$schema` values are unchanged.

Given the repository after the change, When `bash scripts/ci.sh` (including the FR-11 lint) runs, Then it exits 0 and runs the new template tests, backend/package.json has no runtime `dependencies`, backend/plugin/azdo-remote-config.ts is unchanged, and the validator CLI behaviour on the shared example is unchanged (exit 0).

items.title: Bootstrap installer for macOS/Linux (install.sh): plugin copy, personal config, prerequisite check
items.description: FR-18 (install.sh half) / FR-19 / FR-20 / FR-21 / FR-23 / AC-12 / AC-14 for POSIX (macOS, Linux; also runnable under Git Bash for CI). Cycle 0011 PO split: the FR-22 smoke test (fetch shared file + Bifrost /v1/models) moved to F-019 so this slice stays small. Location: backend/installer/install.sh (ADR-0001 layout); the Architect records in an ADR how the installer locates the plugin source (e.g. relative to the script, ../plugin/azdo-remote-config.ts, or an explicit source option) and the personal config template (backend/personal-config/kilo.jsonc). Inputs (PO decision): org, project and repo are REQUIRED (repo has no default since contract 0.5.0) and are given as flags (e.g. --org/--project/--repo) or KILO_AZDO_ORG/PROJECT/REPO env vars; optional path/branch/mode with the plugin defaults. The engineer's virtual key is supplied ONLY via the env var KILO_BIFROST_KEY (never a CLI argument, so it never appears in argv / process listings); when absent, an existing apiKey is kept, or the template placeholder is written for a new config and a message tells the engineer to set it. Editing an existing JSONC personal config (FR-20): the Architect may delegate parsing/editing to a zero-dependency Node helper reusing the plugin's parseJsonc (Kilo CLI ships on npm, so Node is assumed present; the installer checks for it and prints a fix if missing) or another approach; comments in an existing personal config need not be preserved, but a byte-identical timestamped backup is written before any modification. Cycle 0010 security/architect/docs follow-ups: the personal config is written with user-only permissions (0600; ~/.config/kilo/azdo/ not group/world-writable), an existing personal config is never overwritten without a backup, and the plugin entry path ./azdo/azdo-remote-config.ts resolves relative to the Kilo global config dir (~/.config/kilo/, honouring XDG_CONFIG_HOME if the Architect confirms Kilo does). Prerequisites are checked BEFORE anything is written. Tests run install.sh in a child bash process with a temp HOME and a fake PATH containing stub az/node as needed; they never touch the real home directory, network, az or Kilo. The plugin file, its export surface and the validator rules are unchanged. Zero runtime npm deps (FR-11).
acceptance_criteria: Given a temp HOME with no ~/.config/kilo/, org/project/repo supplied, KILO_BIFROST_KEY set and a stub `az` on PATH that reports a logged-in account, When install.sh runs, Then it exits 0, `~/.config/kilo/azdo/azdo-remote-config.ts` is byte-identical to backend/plugin/azdo-remote-config.ts, and `~/.config/kilo/kilo.jsonc` parses with the plugin's `__internals.parseJsonc` to an object with exactly one plugin entry `["./azdo/azdo-remote-config.ts", {...}]` whose org/project/repo equal the supplied values and whose path/branch/mode are `/kilo.jsonc`/`main`/`defaults`, and provider.bifrost.options.apiKey equals KILO_BIFROST_KEY; and on POSIX the personal config's mode is 0600.

Given any run with KILO_BIFROST_KEY set to `sk-bf-AbCdEf1234567890` and AZDO_PAT set to a sentinel value, When the full stdout and stderr of install.sh are captured, Then neither value appears in the output; and Given a fresh HOME and KILO_BIFROST_KEY unset, When install.sh runs, Then apiKey equals the template placeholder `sk-bf-<your-virtual-key>` and the output tells the engineer to set their virtual key.

Given an existing ~/.config/kilo/kilo.jsonc (with comments) containing `model`, `provider.other`, `provider.bifrost.options.headers`, `provider.bifrost.options.apiKey: 'sk-bf-existing'`, another plugin entry `my-other-plugin` and an outdated azdo-remote-config entry, When install.sh runs with KILO_BIFROST_KEY unset, Then every other key deep-equals its previous value, `my-other-plugin` is still present, there is exactly one azdo-remote-config entry carrying the supplied options, apiKey is still `sk-bf-existing`, and a backup file byte-identical to the original exists next to it; and When run with KILO_BIFROST_KEY set, Then apiKey is updated to that value.

Given any install.sh run (fresh or update), When the temp HOME is inspected afterwards, Then nothing exists under `~/.config/kilo/plugin/` that was created by the installer and the personal config references azdo-remote-config.ts exactly once (plugin loads exactly once, AC-12, FR-19).

Given a PATH without `az` and no AZDO_PAT / AZURE_DEVOPS_EXT_PAT / KILO_AZDO_PAT, or a stub `az` whose `account show` exits non-zero, When install.sh runs, Then it exits non-zero, stderr names the fix (install the Azure CLI and run `az login`, or set AZDO_PAT), and no file or directory is created under the temp HOME; and Given no az but AZDO_PAT set, Then the prerequisite check passes (FR-21).

Given install.sh has run successfully once, When it is run a second time with the same inputs, Then it exits 0, and a recursive byte comparison of ~/.config/kilo/ before and after shows no change except (at most) the plugin file, and no additional backup file is created (AC-14, FR-23).

Given missing org, project or repo (no flag and no env var), an unknown flag, or an existing personal config that is not valid JSONC or whose root is not an object, When install.sh runs, Then it exits non-zero with a usage or fixed error message (no stack trace, no file contents echoed) and every pre-existing file under the temp HOME is byte-identical afterwards.

Given the repository after the change, When `bash scripts/ci.sh` (including the FR-11 lint) runs, Then it exits 0 and runs the installer tests (or skips POSIX-permission assertions on Windows with a clear message), backend/package.json has no runtime `dependencies`, and backend/plugin/azdo-remote-config.ts and backend/personal-config/kilo.jsonc are unchanged.

items.title: Bootstrap installer for Windows (install.ps1)
items.description: FR-18 (install.ps1 half) / FR-19..FR-23 / AC-10 (simulated) / AC-12 / AC-14 for Windows, behaviour parity with install.sh (F-010) and its smoke test (F-019). PO decision (cycle 0014): backend/installer/install.ps1 is a THIN front end like install.sh: it parses parameters, applies env/defaults, checks prerequisites, then pipes the NUL-terminated stdin records of contract installer-cli section 4 (org, project, repo, path, branch, mode, apiKey, smoke) to the existing `node install-helper.ts`, whose exit code it returns. All file work, personal-config editing, backups, permissions and the smoke test stay in the shared helper (no second implementation in PowerShell). Parameters: -Org, -Project, -Repo, -Path, -Branch, -Mode, -NoSmoke, -Help (Architect fixes exact names and records them as a contract amendment, e.g. installer-cli 1.2.0); env fallbacks KILO_AZDO_ORG/PROJECT/REPO/PATH/BRANCH/MODE; the virtual key comes ONLY from env KILO_BIFROST_KEY (no parameter, never in argv) and secrets travel on stdin only. Same exit codes 0-4 and same fixed messages as install.sh (script name may read install.ps1). Must run under Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7+ (pwsh), with no module installs (no Pester requirement). Prerequisites (FR-21): node >= 22.18 on PATH; one of AZDO_PAT / AZURE_DEVOPS_EXT_PAT / KILO_AZDO_PAT non-empty, else `az` on PATH and `az account show` succeeding; all checked before anything is written. Plugin path: <config dir>\azdo\azdo-remote-config.ts with config dir from the helper (XDG_CONFIG_HOME or <USERPROFILE>\.config\kilo), referenced as ./azdo/azdo-remote-config.ts. Cycle 0010 security: personal config written user-only (the helper's Windows behaviour is documented by the Architect; no new ACL code required unless the Architect decides otherwise), never overwritten without a backup. Tests: node:test suites under backend/test/installer/ spawn `pwsh -NoProfile -NonInteractive -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File install.ps1` (or powershell.exe when pwsh is absent) with a temp USERPROFILE/HOME, an allow-listed env and stub az/node shims, reusing the F-019 fake-network preload (test/installer/fixtures/fake-network.ts) for smoke cases; when no PowerShell is available the suite skips with a clear message. Tests never touch the real home directory, network, az or Kilo. The plugin file, its export surface, the validator rules, the personal config template and install.sh behaviour are unchanged. Zero runtime npm deps (FR-11).
acceptance_criteria: Given a temp USERPROFILE (and HOME) with no Kilo config, -Org/-Project/-Repo supplied, KILO_BIFROST_KEY set, AZDO_PAT set and -NoSmoke, When install.ps1 runs under PowerShell, Then it exits 0, `<profile>/.config/kilo/azdo/azdo-remote-config.ts` is byte-identical to backend/plugin/azdo-remote-config.ts, and `<profile>/.config/kilo/kilo.jsonc` is byte-identical to the file install.sh produces for the same inputs in another temp home (one plugin entry `["./azdo/azdo-remote-config.ts", {org, project, repo, path:'/kilo.jsonc', branch:'main', mode:'defaults'}]`, apiKey equal to KILO_BIFROST_KEY).

Given org/project/repo/path/branch/mode supplied only through KILO_AZDO_* env vars, and separately both a parameter and an env var for the same setting, When install.ps1 runs, Then env values are used when parameters are absent and the parameter wins when both are set; and Given a missing org, project or repo, an unknown parameter (e.g. -ApiKey or -Key), or a positional argument, When it runs, Then it exits 2 with a usage message that does not echo the offending argument text and nothing is created under the temp profile.

Given an existing personal config (with comments) containing `model`, `provider.other`, `provider.bifrost.options.headers`, apiKey `sk-bf-existing`, a `my-other-plugin` entry and an outdated azdo-remote-config entry, When install.ps1 runs with KILO_BIFROST_KEY unset, Then every other key deep-equals its previous value, `my-other-plugin` is still present, exactly one azdo-remote-config entry carries the supplied options, apiKey is still `sk-bf-existing`, and a backup byte-identical to the original exists next to it (FR-20).

Given any install.ps1 run (fresh or update), When the temp profile is inspected, Then nothing exists under `.config/kilo/plugin/` or `.config/kilo/plugins/` that was created by the installer and the personal config references azdo-remote-config.ts exactly once (FR-19, AC-12); and Given install.ps1 has run successfully once, When it runs a second time with the same inputs, Then it exits 0, a recursive byte comparison of the config dir shows no change except (at most) the plugin file, and no additional backup is created (FR-23, AC-14).

Given a PATH without `az` and no AZDO_PAT / AZURE_DEVOPS_EXT_PAT / KILO_AZDO_PAT, or a stub az whose `account show` exits non-zero, or no node / a node reporting version 22.17.0 on PATH, When install.ps1 runs, Then it exits 1, stderr names the fix (install the Azure CLI and run `az login`, or set AZDO_PAT; install Node.js 22.18 or later), and nothing is created under the temp profile; and Given no az but AZDO_PAT set, Then the prerequisite check passes (FR-21).

Given the F-019 fake network (AzDO Items API serving backend/shared-config/kilo.jsonc, Bifrost GET /v1/models) and smoke enabled, When install.ps1 runs, Then with succeeding fakes it exits 0 and prints `smoke azdo: pass` and `smoke bifrost: pass` with exactly one Bifrost request carrying `Authorization: Bearer <KILO_BIFROST_KEY>`; with Bifrost returning 401 it prints `smoke bifrost: fail 401` and exits 4 leaving the installed files byte-identical to the success run (AC-10 simulated); and with -NoSmoke no smoke request is sent and no `smoke` line is printed.

Given runs on the success, usage-error, prerequisite-failure and smoke-failure paths with KILO_BIFROST_KEY `sk-bf-AbCdEf1234567890` and AZDO_PAT set to a sentinel value, When the full stdout and stderr are captured and the command line of every process spawned by install.ps1 is checked (e.g. via the stub node/az shims recording their argv), Then neither value appears in any output or argv, and install.ps1 has no parameter that accepts a key or PAT.

Given the repository after the change, When `bash scripts/ci.sh` (including the FR-11 lint) runs, Then it exits 0 and runs the install.ps1 tests (or skips them with a clear message when no PowerShell is installed), the existing install.sh, smoke and helper tests still pass, backend/package.json has no runtime `dependencies`, backend/plugin/azdo-remote-config.ts, backend/personal-config/kilo.jsonc and backend/installer/install.sh are unchanged, and docs/architecture/contracts/installer-cli.md documents install.ps1's parameters, env inputs and exit codes.

items.title: End-to-end simulated startup test
items.description: Vision AC-1 / AC-2 / AC-3 / AC-4 / AC-6 / AC-7 / AC-9 / AC-10 / AC-12, simulated end to end (startup sequence steps 1-7). Cycle 0016 PO: priority raised to 2 (critical path; last vision verification slice before docs). TEST-ONLY item: a new node:test suite (PO default backend/test/e2e/; Architect fixes the location and records the harness design in an ADR or contract note) that chains the shipped pieces exactly as an engineer's machine would: (1) run backend/installer/install.sh in a child bash process with a temp HOME (and USERPROFILE), an allow-listed env, AZDO_PAT and KILO_BIFROST_KEY set (so no az is needed); (2) a test-only 'Kilo start simulator' (child Node process, test code under backend/test/, never product code) that reads the INSTALLED personal config `<home>/.config/kilo/kilo.jsonc` with the plugin's parseJsonc, resolves each plugin entry path relative to the Kilo global config dir, dynamically imports the INSTALLED plugin file `<home>/.config/kilo/azdo/azdo-remote-config.ts` (not the backend/ source), calls its default export's `server(input, options)` with the entry's options and a capturing fake logger, runs the returned `config` hook on the parsed personal config, and writes the resulting config and captured log records to a file/stdout for assertions. Network is faked with the F-019 preload (backend/test/installer/fixtures/fake-network.ts via --import, scenario file per start); the Architect may extend that fixture (e.g. a Bifrost answer that returns 401 unless `Authorization: Bearer <expected key>` matches, and a way to change the AzDO content between starts) but it stays under backend/test/. The plugin reads its cache from `<temp home>/.cache/kilo-azdo/`; tests never touch the real home directory, real network, real az or real Kilo. When bash is unavailable the suite skips with a clear message. Product files (backend/plugin/, backend/validator/, backend/installer/, backend/personal-config/, backend/shared-config/, backend/tools/) are NOT changed; if a product defect is found the engineer records it as a finding instead of weakening the test. Zero runtime npm deps (FR-11).
acceptance_criteria: Given a fresh temp HOME, install.sh run with --org/--project/--repo, AZDO_PAT, KILO_BIFROST_KEY and --no-smoke, and a fake AzDO Items API serving backend/shared-config/kilo.jsonc, When the Kilo start simulator loads the installed personal config and the installed plugin and runs its config hook, Then the resulting config has provider.bifrost.options.baseURL equal to the shared value, provider.bifrost.models with keys `azure/gpt-5` and `azure/gpt-5-mini`, provider.bifrost.options.apiKey equal to KILO_BIFROST_KEY, and exactly one AzDO request was sent to the dev.azure.com Items API with the installed org/project/repo, path `/kilo.jsonc`, branch `main` and api-version=7.1 (AC-1, simulated).

Given the installed personal config, When the simulator resolves its plugin entries, Then exactly one entry resolves to `<home>/.config/kilo/azdo/azdo-remote-config.ts`, the plugin server is invoked exactly once per simulated start, and nothing exists under `<home>/.config/kilo/plugin/` or `plugins/` (AC-12).

Given a first successful simulated start, When the shared file served by the fake AzDO is changed (e.g. a new model `azure/gpt-5-nano` added and a top-level `small_model` value changed) and the simulator starts again with no installer re-run, Then the new model and value are in effect, every other resulting key deep-equals the first start's result, the personal config and installed plugin file are byte-identical to before, and `<home>/.cache/kilo-azdo/remote-config.json` holds the new shared content (AC-2).

Given a successful start has written the cache, When the next start's fake AzDO fails (request throws, and separately returns HTTP 500), Then the resulting config deep-equals the result of the successful start and a warn-level record with service `azdo-remote-config` was logged; and Given a fresh install with no cache and a failing fake AzDO, When the simulator starts, Then the resulting config deep-equals the installed personal config as parsed (local config only), an error-level record was logged, and the simulator exits 0 (AC-3, AC-4, FR-10).

items.title: Bootstrap installer smoke test (install.sh)
items.description: FR-22 / AC-10 (simulated), split out of F-010 in cycle 0011. After a successful install (exit 0 path of contract installer-cli 1.0.0), install.sh runs a smoke test with two checks: (1) `azdo`: fetch the shared file with the plugin's own `__internals.fetchRemoteConfig` (same URL, PAT/az-token rules and fixed error codes as FR-2/FR-3; no second HTTP/auth implementation) and parse it with `__internals.parseJsonc`; (2) `bifrost`: GET `<provider.bifrost.options.baseURL>/models` (baseURL from the fetched shared config, trailing slash normalised; with the Appendix A value this is `https://bifrost.yourcompany.internal/v1/models`) with `Authorization: Bearer <apiKey>` where apiKey is the value now in the personal config. PO decisions (conservative): the key is never sent over non-https, so a non-https or unparseable baseURL makes the bifrost check fail with a fixed code without any request; when the personal config still holds the template placeholder `sk-bf-<your-virtual-key>` (no key set) the bifrost check reports `skipped` with a message to set KILO_BIFROST_KEY and sends nothing; when the azdo check fails the bifrost check is `skipped`. Each request is bounded by the plugin timeout (settings.timeoutMs, default 5000 ms) and response bodies are capped (1 MiB). Exit codes (contract amendment, Architect records it): 0 = installed and every check passed or was skipped; 4 = installed but at least one smoke check failed; a failed smoke test NEVER undoes or modifies the installation. A `--no-smoke` flag skips the smoke test (for offline machines and for the existing F-010 installer tests, which must not touch the network). Output is one line per check: `smoke <check>: pass|fail|skipped [<fixed code or HTTP status>]`. Test seam (Architect decides; PO suggestion): the smoke logic lives in a pure module under backend/installer/ with injectable fetch/runAz/env, unit-tested with fakes, plus child-process tests of install.sh that replace globalThis.fetch via a test-only preload (e.g. NODE_OPTIONS=--import <fixture>) or local fake HTTP servers; no product-level option may redirect the AzDO host or relax the https rule. Tests never touch the real network, az, Kilo or home directory. The plugin file and its export surface, the validator rules and the personal config template are unchanged. Zero runtime npm deps (FR-11).
acceptance_criteria: Given a temp HOME, valid org/project/repo, AZDO_PAT set, KILO_BIFROST_KEY set, a fake AzDO Items API returning the shipped example shared config (backend/shared-config/kilo.jsonc) and a fake Bifrost returning 200 for GET /v1/models, When install.sh runs, Then it exits 0, prints `smoke azdo: pass` and `smoke bifrost: pass`, the AzDO request was made via the plugin's fetchRemoteConfig URL rules (dev.azure.com Items API, api-version=7.1, the configured path/branch), and exactly one Bifrost request was sent to `https://bifrost.yourcompany.internal/v1/models` carrying `Authorization: Bearer <KILO_BIFROST_KEY>`.

Given the fake Bifrost returns 401 (AC-10, simulated) or the fake AzDO returns 404, When install.sh runs, Then the failing check prints `fail` with the HTTP status (e.g. `smoke bifrost: fail 401`, `smoke azdo: fail http-404`), when azdo fails the bifrost check is reported `skipped` and no Bifrost request is sent, the script exits 4, and the personal config and plugin file are byte-identical to those of a successful run with the same inputs (installation is not undone).

Given a fetch that never responds, or a fetched shared file that is invalid JSONC, has no string provider.bifrost.options.baseURL, or has an `http://` or unparseable baseURL, When the smoke test runs, Then the relevant check fails with a fixed code (e.g. timeout, invalid-jsonc, no-base-url, insecure-base-url) within a bounded time (timeoutMs), no request carrying the virtual key is sent to a non-https URL, and the script exits 4.

Given a fresh HOME with KILO_BIFROST_KEY unset (personal config holds the placeholder `sk-bf-<your-virtual-key>`), When install.sh runs with succeeding fakes, Then the bifrost check is reported `skipped` with a message telling the engineer to set KILO_BIFROST_KEY, no Bifrost request is sent, and the script exits 0; and Given an existing personal config with apiKey `sk-bf-existing` and KILO_BIFROST_KEY unset, Then the Bifrost request carries `Bearer sk-bf-existing`.

Given no PAT from any source and a stub az that returns a token, When the smoke test runs, Then the AzDO request carries `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (same rules as FR-3 through fetchRemoteConfig) and the Bifrost request carries only the virtual key, never the az token or PAT.

Given smoke test runs on the success, 401, 404, timeout and exception paths with KILO_BIFROST_KEY `sk-bf-AbCdEf1234567890`, AZDO_PAT and an az token set to sentinel values, When the full stdout and stderr are captured, Then none of those values (nor the base64 Basic credential) appears, and no error message text from fetch or the response body is echoed.

Given `--no-smoke`, When install.sh runs, Then no HTTP request and no az token call for the smoke test is made, no `smoke` line is printed and the exit code follows the F-010 contract; and Given an install that fails before writing (exit 1, 2 or 3), Then the smoke test does not run.

Given the repository after the change, When `bash scripts/ci.sh` (including the FR-11 lint) runs, Then it exits 0, runs the new smoke-test tests and the existing F-010 installer tests (which make no real network call), backend/package.json has no runtime `dependencies`, backend/plugin/azdo-remote-config.ts and backend/personal-config/kilo.jsonc are unchanged, and docs/architecture/contracts/installer-cli.md documents the smoke test output, exit code 4 and `--no-smoke`.

items.title: Bind cache to the settings that produced it
items.description: Cycle 0008 security low 1: the cache (~/.cache/kilo-azdo/remote-config.json, FR-7) is one fixed file not linked to org/project/repo/path/branch, so on fetch failure a cache written for another org or repo can be applied. Store a non-secret settings fingerprint (org, project, repo, path, branch; never the PAT or any token) with the cached config and verify it on read; apply the cache only on an exact match. Scope (cycle 0019): plugin cache write/read and hook fallback in backend/plugin/azdo-remote-config.ts, its tests, and the plugin-interface contract section 2f (cache file format). The ADR-0009 question (can a Kilo project-level config override the global plugin options) is split out to T-029 because it needs a real Kilo and cannot be verified by an automated test.

Given a cache written for settings S, When the hook runs again with identical settings S and the fetch fails, Then the cached config is applied exactly as before this change (AC-3 / FR-7 behaviour preserved) and the existing 'using cached config' warning is logged.

Given a successful fetch with a PAT supplied via options or env, When the cache file is written, Then the file contains the binding fields (org, project, repo, path, branch) and the shared config, and does NOT contain the PAT value, any Authorization/bearer token, or the az access token (asserted by searching the written bytes for the test secret values).

Given a legacy cache file in the pre-change format (bare shared-config object with no binding) or a cache whose binding is malformed (missing field, wrong type), When the fetch fails, Then the cache is treated as unusable (not applied, never throws), and When the next fetch succeeds, Then the cache is rewritten in the new bound format.

Given required settings are missing (org, project or repo unset), When the hook runs and a cache exists, Then the cache is not applied (no binding can be verified), the existing missing-settings warning is logged, and the hook completes without throwing with the config unchanged.

Given binding values that differ only by letter case or surrounding whitespace, When the fetch fails, Then the outcome follows the comparison rule documented in the plugin-interface contract (exact match on the values as normalised by resolveSettings) and a test pins that rule.

Given the full suite, When `bash scripts/ci.sh` runs, Then it exits 0, the plugin remains one TypeScript file with zero runtime npm dependencies (FR-11), and the e2e simulated startup test still passes its cache-fallback scenario.
items.notes: Selected in cycle 0019. items.title: Installer hardening: CDPATH-safe helper lookup, symlink re-check, Node version test fix
items.description: Cycle 0011 security+review follow-ups for backend/installer, trimmed in cycle 0020 to the items with real value. IN SCOPE: (1, review low 2 / sec low 2) install.sh resolves script_dir with `cd "$script_dir" && pwd`; when CDPATH is set and the script is invoked via a relative path containing '/', bash cd searches CDPATH and echoes the directory, so script_dir can be wrong or multi-line and the hand-off to install-helper.ts breaks. (2, sec low 1) install-helper.ts applyPlan: after mkdirSync(azdoDir) and before any chmod/write in configDir/azdoDir (including the no-change chmod of kilo.jsonc), re-lstat configDir, azdoDir and the config file and refuse (existing fixed refusal message/exit code per installer contract) if any became a symlink, never following it. items.title: Installer smoke test: network pre-flight for Azure IP firewall / VPN before any credential is sent
items.description: USER requirement (cycle 0022): the Bifrost gateway (and possibly other Kilo-facing endpoints) sit behind an Azure IP firewall / IP allow-list. An engineer who is not on the VPN or whose public IP is not allow-listed today gets a confusing smoke failure (timeout, reset, or HTTP 403 that reads like a bad key) and the virtual key / AzDO credential is sent anyway. Add a pre-flight 'network' check to backend/installer/smoke.ts (shared by install.sh and install.ps1) that runs BEFORE the authenticated Azure DevOps fetch and BEFORE GET <baseURL>/models: one unauthenticated, bounded HTTPS probe per target (the fixed Azure DevOps host https://dev.azure.com/ and the origin of the validated https Bifrost baseURL). Classification (fixed, value-free codes): HTTP 403 or 407 -> '<target>-blocked'; network error (DNS, refused, reset, TLS) -> '<target>-unreachable'; deadline -> '<target>-timeout'; any other HTTP status (2xx, 3xx, 401, 404, 5xx...) -> reachable (rationale: an allowed client that sends no credentials normally gets 401/404/redirect, whereas an Azure firewall / Front Door / App Service access restriction answers 403 or drops the connection). target is 'azdo' or 'bifrost'. When a target fails the probe, its authenticated check is skipped with code 'network-blocked' and the credential for it is never sent. Output adds a first line 'smoke network: pass' or 'smoke network: fail <code>[,<code>]' and, on failure, one fixed hint line: connect to the corporate VPN or ask the platform team to add your public IP to the Azure firewall allow-list, then re-run <front end>. Exit code stays 4 when the network check fails. No new runtime dependencies; plugin file untouched; tests use injected fake fetch / clock only (never real network, az, or home).
acceptance_criteria: Given a fake fetch where the unauthenticated probes of https://dev.azure.com/ and of the Bifrost baseURL origin answer with a non-403/407 HTTP status (e.g. 200, 302, 401, 404), When runSmoke runs, Then report.network is pass, formatSmoke prints 'smoke network: pass' as the first line, and the azdo and bifrost authenticated checks run and are reported exactly as before.

Given a fake fetch whose probe of the Bifrost origin answers HTTP 403, When runSmoke runs, Then the network line is 'smoke network: fail bifrost-blocked', bifrost is 'skipped network-blocked', the fake records no request to <baseURL>/models and no request carrying the virtual key, the fixed VPN / IP allow-list hint line naming the front end is printed, and smokeFailed returns true (installer exit code 4).

Given a fake fetch whose probe of https://dev.azure.com/ rejects with a network error, or never settles until a fake clock passes timeoutMs, When runSmoke runs, Then the network code is 'azdo-unreachable' or 'azdo-timeout' respectively, the fake az runner is never invoked, no PAT or bearer token is sent, azdo is 'skipped network-blocked', and runSmoke resolves (never hangs, never rejects).

Given any probe, When the fake fetch records it, Then it is a GET (or HEAD) to an https: origin only (no path beyond '/', no query), with redirect 'manual', an AbortSignal, no body, and no Authorization, api-key, x-api-key or Cookie header.

Given a missing, invalid or non-https baseURL, or no key / a key reference, When runSmoke runs, Then the Bifrost probe is not sent and the existing bifrost codes (no-base-url, invalid-base-url, insecure-base-url, no-key, key-reference) are reported unchanged; and Given --no-smoke, Then no probe or other network call is made.

Given any probe outcome (including a probe response whose body contains a key-like or HTML string, or an internal exception), When the report is formatted, Then every printed line comes from the fixed code set and contains no key, PAT, token, baseURL, host name or response body text; an internal error yields 'smoke network: fail internal' instead of a throw.

Given the same blocked fake for front ends 'install.sh' and 'install.ps1', When formatSmoke runs, Then both produce identical network and hint lines except the front-end name, and all existing smoke, installer and e2e tests still pass with 'bash scripts/ci.sh' exiting 0.

items.title: Plugin: classify Azure firewall / network-blocked failures in the remote fetch with an actionable log hint
items.description: USER requirement (cycle 0022, verbatim: 'my current KILO and Bifrost URL is running behind AZURE IP firewall, so we need to make sure that is validated before we fetch the URL as that will cause error'), plugin side. fetchRemoteConfig today reports 'network', 'timeout' or 'http-<status>', so a firewall / IP allow-list / corporate proxy block of the Azure DevOps fetch looks like an auth problem or a generic error. Cycle 0023 PO decisions (no human available): (1) NO unauthenticated probe in the plugin - it runs inside Kilo at every start, a probe would add a second round trip to every startup, and the authenticated fetch's own failure already carries the signal; the PAT / az token only ever goes to the fixed https://dev.azure.com/ host over TLS. Classification is done on the single existing authenticated fetch within the single existing timeoutMs budget, still exactly one fetch call per hook run. (2) New fixed, value-free FetchErrorCode values: 'network-unreachable' = the fetch() call itself rejects before the deadline (DNS, refused, reset, TLS). 'network-blocked' = HTTP 407 (proxy auth; Azure DevOps itself never answers 407) with any body, or HTTP 403 whose Content-Type is absent, unreadable or not JSON (media type before ';', trimmed, case-insensitive, is neither 'application/json' nor ends with '+json'), i.e. the HTML / plain-text page of a firewall, proxy, WAF or Front Door. Azure DevOps answers real permission failures with a JSON 403, which stays 'http-403'; 401 always stays 'http-401'. Decision is made from the status and the Content-Type header only; the body is never read or inspected (discarded unread exactly as today), so no response text can reach a log. 'timeout' is unchanged (a deadline is still 'timeout', also when fetch rejects after the deadline). 'network' remains the catch-all for a missing fetch, an unexpected internal throw and a body-stream failure after headers arrived (the connection was open, so not a firewall). (3) Config hook: the existing 'Remote config unavailable (<code>) ...' lines are unchanged in format; in addition exactly ONE fixed warn-level hint line is logged right after it: NETWORK hint for network-unreachable, network-blocked and timeout (a silently dropping firewall shows up as a timeout), e.g. 'Azure DevOps could not be reached from this network: connect to the corporate VPN or ask the platform team to allow your public IP, then restart Kilo.'; CREDENTIALS hint for http-401, http-403 and auth-unavailable, e.g. 'Azure DevOps rejected or lacks credentials: run az login or replace your PAT, and check your access to the shared config repository.'; no hint for any other code. Exact texts are pinned by the Architect in the plugin-interface contract and contain no values (no URL, host, org/project/repo, PAT, token, header or body). (4) Cache order unchanged (ADR-0008: remote first, cache only on failure) - a cache-first order would serve stale enforce-mode config and is not requested. Cache fallback (AC-3 / FR-7) and the T-013 / ADR-0018 settings binding are unchanged. (5) FR-10 never throws, FR-11 one TypeScript file with zero runtime deps and no new import, no new __internals key, AC-9 no secret in any log. The installer smoke (smoke.ts) passes plugin codes through unchanged, so 'smoke azdo: fail network-unreachable' / 'network-blocked' can appear only when the F-020 probe passed but the authenticated fetch failed; smoke.ts needs no code change. Scope: backend/plugin/azdo-remote-config.ts, backend/test/plugin/*, the e2e/smoke tests that pin the old 'network' text for a fetch rejection, plugin-interface contract (+ ADR or ADR-0007 amendment). User-facing docs are F-022.
acceptance_criteria: Given a fake fetch whose call rejects (connection error) before the deadline, When fetchRemoteConfig runs with a PAT or az token, Then it resolves { ok: false, error: 'network-unreachable' }; and Given a fake fetch that never settles until a fake clock passes timeoutMs (or rejects after the deadline fired), Then the error is still 'timeout'; and Given no usable fetch function, an unexpected internal throw, or a body stream that fails after a 2xx status, Then the error is still 'network'.

Given a fake fetch answering HTTP 407 (any Content-Type), or HTTP 403 with Content-Type absent, 'text/html; charset=utf-8', 'text/plain', or a headers.get that throws or returns a non-string, When fetchRemoteConfig runs, Then it resolves { ok: false, error: 'network-blocked' }, the body's getReader is never called and body.cancel is invoked (body discarded unread, as for any non-2xx).

Given a fake fetch answering HTTP 403 with Content-Type 'application/json', 'Application/JSON; charset=utf-8' or 'application/problem+json', or HTTP 401 with any Content-Type (including text/html), When fetchRemoteConfig runs, Then the error is 'http-403' / 'http-401' respectively; and every other non-2xx status (e.g. 404, 500, 503) still yields 'http-<status>' exactly as before.

Given the config hook and a fetch failure with code network-unreachable, network-blocked or timeout, When the hook runs, Then the existing 'Remote config unavailable (<code>) ...' line is logged unchanged in format followed by exactly one warn-level line equal to the fixed NETWORK hint constant (VPN / ask the platform team to allow your public IP); Given http-401, http-403 (JSON) or auth-unavailable, Then exactly one warn line equal to the fixed CREDENTIALS hint (az login / PAT / repository access) and no network hint; Given any other code (http-404, http-5xx, too-large, bad-response, network, invalid-settings, a validation error), Then no hint line is logged.

Given a valid cache bound to the current settings (T-013) and a fetch failing with network-unreachable or network-blocked, When the hook runs, Then the cached config is merged exactly as before, the 'Remote config unavailable (<code>); using cached config.' warning and the NETWORK hint are logged, and the fake fetch was called exactly once (no extra probe request, remote-first order of ADR-0008 unchanged); Given a cache bound to different settings, Then it is not applied (cache-mismatch) and the config object is unchanged.

Given failures whose fake response carries canary values in the body, in the Content-Type and other headers, and a PAT / az token canary, When the hook runs (including with throwing header getters and a throwing log sink), Then runConfigHook resolves without throwing and no log line contains the PAT, token, Authorization value, URL, host name, org/project/repo values, any header value or any body text.

Given the plugin after the change, When the FR-11 lint and 'bash scripts/ci.sh' run, Then the plugin is still ONE TypeScript file with zero runtime npm dependencies and no new import, the __internals key set is unchanged, the installer smoke reports a plugin-side code verbatim (a reachable F-020 probe followed by a rejecting authenticated fetch gives 'smoke azdo: fail network-unreachable'), existing tests change only where a fetch rejection's code moved from 'network' to 'network-unreachable', and CI exits 0.
